findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false; logic is dead/confusing and could be misread as a bug to be fixed later
findings.body: The new function `enableSqlExpressions` reads `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` in both branches of the subsequent `if`. The function is therefore equivalent to `return false`, regardless of the `FlagSqlExpressions` feature toggle. This is the correct security outcome (SQL expressions are always disabled, even if an admin re-enables the feature flag, so the flag cannot be used to bring back the vulnerable code path), but the implementation is misleading: the variable is named `enabled` but actually represents the inverted/disabled state, and the feature-flag check is effectively dead code. A future maintainer who reads this as "this is broken, the last return should be true" would silently re-introduce the CVE-2024-9264 RCE/LFI path. The function should either be a single `return false` with a comment explaining the CVE-related permanent disablement, or it should make the unconditional disablement explicit (e.g., `return false // SQL Expressions permanently disabled; see CVE-2024-9264`). As written, it is both confusing and a latent footgun for a critical security control.

findings.title: Error string "sqlExpressions is not implemented" misleads users and operators
findings.body: When a panel using a SQL expression is evaluated, the user now sees `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. SQL Expressions are fully implemented in this codebase — they have been deliberately disabled to mitigate CVE-2024-9264 (RCE/LFI via DuckDB). Saying "not implemented" will mislead end users into thinking it is a bug or a missing feature, and will make incident triage harder (operators will search for an unimplemented feature rather than a security disablement). The error should clearly state that SQL Expressions have been disabled for security reasons (and ideally reference the CVE / blog post so admins and users understand why).

findings.title: No automated test asserts that SQL Expressions are disabled and return the expected error
findings.body: This is a critical-severity security fix that introduces a new code path in `ReadQuery` (the `QueryTypeSQL` branch returning an error) and replaces the DuckDB-backed `pkg/expr/sql` implementation with stubs returning "not implemented". Despite being a security control, the PR adds no tests. At a minimum there should be a unit test in `pkg/expr` that exercises `ReadQuery` / `ExpressionQueryReader` with a `QueryTypeSQL` payload and asserts that the returned error matches the intended message, plus a test that `sql.TablesList` and `(*SQLCommand).Execute` no longer execute any SQL. Without these tests, a future refactor could silently re-enable the feature (e.g., by "fixing" the broken `enableSqlExpressions` logic or by re-introducing a real DuckDB dependency) and there would be no automated signal.

findings.title: Dead method (*DB).TablesList is never called
findings.body: The new stub `DB` in `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` defines a `TablesList(rawSQL string) ([]string, error)` method, but neither `parser.go` nor `sql_command.go` ever invokes `db.TablesList` — they call `RunCommands` and `QueryFramesInto` respectively. This method is unreachable dead code that adds a public-looking API surface to the stub package. It should be removed (or, if it is intended to be the replacement for the package-level `sql.TablesList`, that should actually be wired up to use it instead of going through `RunCommands`).
